page: Vultr voc-c-8c-16gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a local 150 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results show strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, Geekbench scores, and memory bandwidth tests consistently fall within the average range. The server achieves a static web serving throughput of 8.57 GB/sec and handles 15.55 million Redis SET operations per second. For machine learning tasks, LLM inference using a medium 7B model yields average text generation speeds of 15.99 tokens per second, though prompt processing is relatively weak at 25.18 tokens per second.

With its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a stable compute-to-memory balance without the performance fluctuations of shared-core options. This resource density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It is suited for web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks.
